core.headline: End-of-terrace Victorian cottage in Smarden conservation area
core.listing:
An end-of-terrace Victorian cottage dating from c.1880, built of red brick under a clay-tiled roof. Number 2 Forge Cottages stands within the Smarden Conservation Area and offers two bedrooms, a bathroom and a cottage garden.

The sitting room measures 3.90m x 3.60m (12'10" x 11'10") and has a cast-iron fireplace. The kitchen/dining room measures 4.30m x 3.20m (14'1" x 10'6") and has a quarry-tiled floor, a range alcove and reclaimed beams. Ledged-and-braced doors are fitted throughout.

On the first floor, bedroom one measures 3.80m x 3.30m (12'6" x 10'10") and bedroom two measures 2.90m x 2.40m (9'6" x 7'10"). The bathroom serves both bedrooms.

The rear cottage garden extends approximately 12m (40ft) and has a brick path and a timber shed.

Smarden village has a pub approximately 2 minutes' walk from the property.

Guide Price £425,000. Freehold. Council Tax Band C (Ashford Borough Council). EPC rating E. Construction: Standard – Red brick under a clay-tiled roof. Electricity: Mains. Water: Mains (not metered). Sewerage: Septic tank. Heating: Oil-fired central heating. Broadband: FTTC. Mobile signal: Good outdoors, variable indoors. Parking: On-street. Building safety: None known. Restrictions: within the Smarden Conservation Area. Rights & easements: septic tank shared with 1 Forge Cottages and located in its garden; access rights for maintenance; emptying costs shared. Flooding: rear of garden in Flood Zone 2 (Environment Agency map); the house has not flooded. Coastal erosion: None known. Planning: None known. Accessibility: None known. Coalfield / mining: None known. Known issues: Seller does not know whether the shared septic tank meets the Environment Agency's 2020 general binding rules. Restricted head height at top of stairs, approx. 1.88m (6'2").
